utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good afternoon to everyone, after a long period in which there were no hearings. As the parties may be aware of, Judge Hanoteau has filed a certificate that he familiarised himself with the case. To the extent that the parties would be surprised by Judge Hanoteau sitting to my right and Judge Canivell sitting to my left, which is not something you would expect, I would explain to you that the right ear of Judge Canivell is far better than his left ear. So it is for practical reasons that we are not acting in accordance with what we traditionally do. I would first like to give Judge Hanoteau an opportunity to address the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Orie. I wanted to say a few words, very briefly. First of all, I wanted to tell you what an honour it is for me to be here today, to be sitting here. I wanted to say as well that it is a great pleasure for me to greet the Prosecutor as well as the Defence counsel. It is also a great pleasure for me to be able to say hello to those who work here. I've read the case file over these past few weeks, and I've understood the level of effort that has been deployed here by everyone in order for this Tribunal to be able to function properly. It is a great pleasure for me to be able to work with you all. Thank you very much for your attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Hanoteau. Today, we have mainly a housekeeping session. One second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This housekeeping session will take approximately the first hour of this afternoon's session. After the break, the parties will be given an opportunity to give oral argument on the motion for adjournment. The parties have received an agenda for this housekeeping session, so I take it that we can go through it relatively quickly. But before we start for the first item of the agenda, I would like to turn to private session for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session now again. We've reached point 3 of the agenda, a decision to be taken on the cross-examination of Witness 63. The Chamber has allowed, on the 10th of December, the Defence to cross-examine Witness 63 on a small range of topics. The Defence has informed the Chamber what topics they wanted to cross-examine the witness on, that is, Trnopolje camp, the matters of access to that camp; Omarska camp, an interview with the journalist, local SDS leaders, their actions, positions and responsibilities, and attempts by Muslims to organise military defence; and finally, as a last issue, the SDA involvement and SDS arming of the population. The Chamber decides that there will be, as was already decided, there will be cross-examination on these issues, and the Office of the Prosecutor is instructed to schedule for that cross-examination. Then we come to a long list -- no, that's not a long list. The translations to be provided by the OTP to the Chamber. The revised translations are expected on P335, P237, P292.1, P330.1, P332, P333, P338, P350.1, P428, P429A. I do understand that these translations can be provided to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, they can be. In respect of 292.1, however, I was reviewing those translations today, this morning, and in respect to 292.1, KID 31469, in looking at the revision of the translation, I concluded that additional clarification is needed, so we are not prepared to submit at this point in time KID 292 -- I'm sorry, Prosecution Exhibit 292.1 KID 31469. We will be able to do so in the upcoming days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we leave that particular topic, I might just indicate in relation to P220 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I did not raise that one specifically because I was informed that the Defence was supplied with an unrevised version of P220. That's the reason why I didn't mention it. Has this been settled meanwhile?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, in respect of 220, we are prepared to submit -- tender today, revised copies of P220.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But has the Defence -- because that was the issue, had not been provided at an earlier stage with the revised translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: They were provided with a revised translation today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Today. Ms. Loukas, how much time would you need to review that revised P220 --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I checked with the case manager just prior to coming into court and at that stage we hadn't received it. I don't know if it's gone into the locker since we've been in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I say you would be ready in two days?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there would be an earlier occasion, please tell us. So from the list we had under agenda item 4, P220 is still pending, and P292.1 KID 34169 is still pending. The others will be tendered. And no objection from the Defence for those?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, there's just one further matter in relation to that series of last numbers, and that's P292.1. It was indicated in the various e-mails that went between the Trial Chamber, the Prosecution, and the Defence, that we had in fact received a binder of material relating to that on the 10th of February, 2005, and I can indicate that we have not received that binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, as I said, I take it that the parties will communicate on P292.1 is still pending at this moment, as is P220. And the others, no objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I just wanted to raise those two parties, the P220 and the P292.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I intervene for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: P292 is an exhibit of intercepted communications that was already before this Court. There are other matters to be resolved in respect of Prosecution Exhibit 292. We haven't touched upon those. Mr. Kljuc is due to come back to finish his cross-examination, and it may be that the best time to regulate the issues relating to 292, is at the conclusion of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So 292.1 will be pending -- both awaiting the reappearance of Mr. Kljuc and any further discussions between the parties.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then that means that P235, P237, P330.1, P332, P333, P338, P350.1, P428, and P429A are admitted into evidence. Then we have P252 as next on our list --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wasn't sure whether Your Honour had meant to skip over item 4 on the agenda, or whether -- I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One of the things I was a bit worried about in the beginning, and that's the reason why I asked the legal officer, is whether we are working exactly from the same agenda, because I might have an internal agenda in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That was simply why I asked, Your Honours, so that we could just know where we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check that we have the same agenda.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will not skip it, but I'll come to that at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could deal with it right away, having the -- this is an amendment to the original agenda where number 4 is included. I do understand that, although not full agreement, that, to some extent, agreement was reached on the statement of Mr. Bjelobrk. The Chamber would like to receive the redacted version of this statement, and on the remaining issues, that is, those parties where the parties could not agree, we'll give a decision in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I comment on that. Before Your Honours give a decision, we do have quite a quantity of material in relation to this witness that was received from Mr. Krajisnik. Your Honour may remember, in fact, it was originally provided direct to the Trial Chamber, and the Trial Chamber very kindly gave it back to us promptly. But, Your Honour, it's quite a lot of material, and we have not so far been able to fully consider that material, so Your Honour may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you'd prefer for us to wait a while and not just act on the basis of the agreed parts, but to give an opportunity at a later stage for the Defence to add anything to the request.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, please, Your Honour, because, although, of course, we don't, and Your Honours won't want to leave things just on ice for longer than necessary, there isn't any special urgency about this particular matter. And we are grateful for that opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When do you think you could be finished with studying the material you received?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, I -- because it's all in B/C/S, I'm not personally going to be the one that's reviewing it first, Your Honour, so I'm ever so slightly reluctant to give a firm timetable on that. It was discussed this morning between myself and Ms. Cmeric and that raises other practical issues as well. Your Honour, may I simply ask that I perhaps can report back on that by the end of the week, and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- and then indicate to Your Honours where we are, and perhaps we can consider how much time is needed. Would that be acceptable to Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is acceptable to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we go to the next issue of -- agenda item 5(a), that is P252. The Defence was supposed to give to the OTP the details of the objections in respect of P252. Has this been done meanwhile?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the note -- I hope Your Honour doesn't mind, the note that I made on my copy of the agenda when it said the Trial Chamber was to remind the Defence, was that we are reminded, Your Honour. I can't, really, I'm afraid, do more than say we are reminded, therefore, and we will take care of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would it be possible -- I mean, it's a matter of just drawing the attention to the objections in respect of the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a video, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a video --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But the problem is, again, we only have one person who can watch the video in any sensible way, apart from seeing what's simply moving on the screen, and it's quite a long video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you report back, well, let's say - I don't think it's a very urgent matter - three weeks, would that do?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's entirely acceptable. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we come to the next -- the next list, which is P347, P395, P396, P399, P402, and P406. The latest information we got is that the Defence had not yet received the response of the OTP in relation to P395, P396, and P399, but that the Prosecution would try to deal also with these exhibits not later than the 28th of February.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can indicate that I was informed by Ms. Cmeric, prior to coming to court, that we received those items today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. How much time would you need to review them, Ms. Loukas? Two days for the ...

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, yes, Your Honour, in view of the fact that this is material relating to Mr. Bjelobrk, I think it would be appropriate to leave this material until the remainder of the Bjelobrk material that we've already referred to is dealt with as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means that you will report back by the end of this week.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so the roared is clear, it's my understanding that three of the documents were submitted prior to today, and three were submitted today, so all six were not received today. But we accept --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but I think we just mentioned 395, 396, and 399 as the ones that the OTP still had to provide them. I didn't mention all six.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, those were the ones I was referring to. The others had been received previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I understood. Then we have three documents, P419, yes, P427, and P458, where the Office of the Prosecution was expected to submit revised translations, that, at least, is valid for 419 and 458, and a new copy of P427 to the Trial Chamber. Are they available, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: They are, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections to the admission of these newly provided documents? And I take it that they have been provided to the Defence before?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, 427 is an issue of replacing only an exhibit that's in the record. It's not a question of a new translation, it's replacing the B/C/S translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think I said that, revised translations. I said at least that is valid for 419 and 458, and a new copy of P427.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, did you receive --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, just in relation to that, Your Honour, we have, of course, previously received P419 and P427, but as I understand it, we have not received P458 as yet. And I think we're hoping to receive it today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you need time to review them. Then for P458, we'll grant you an additional two days. Is that -- would that be sufficient?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, I'm not entirely certain, I must say, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tell me how much you need.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I'd rather leave that for longer, for a week, in view of the fact that, as our case manager, Ms. Cmeric, has a lot of matters to attend to prior to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So for 458, we'll receive your report at the end of this week. And are there any objections against 419 and a newly submitted 427?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I can indicate that we acknowledge receipt of all of them. In terms of an overall confirmation that we have checked all the translations, again, there may be some later time at which a translation revision may need to be made. But at this stage, there are no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Then P419 and P427 are, in a new revised edition, admitted into evidence, and we'll hear further reports on P458 by the Defence no later than the end of this week. Then item 6 on the agenda, translations of D29 and D32 to be provided by the Defence. Are they available, Ms. Loukas or Mr. Stewart?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's D29 and D32.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I can indicate that, yes, they are available, and I have, in fact, got 12 copies of each.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it, then, that they have not yet been provided to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: As far as I understand, no, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would two days be sufficient for the Prosecution to review them?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It will be sufficient, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then on P -- on D29 and D32, we'll hear within the next two days from the Prosecution whether there are any further objections. And then we come to ...

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's D32, and this one is D29.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The numbers have been put on the documents, I take it? Okay. Then we come to agenda item 7(a), the Dzambasovic 92 bis package. Is there a new version of this package available to be tendered, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I understand it has been provided to the registrar already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any -- I take it that they have been provided as well to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The package provided was composed on the basis of an agreement between the parties. May I, therefore, take it that there's no objection against the 92 bis package as provided to the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you please inform us, since the 92 bis material receives exhibit numbers now as well, what are the exhibit numbers of this Dzambasovic package?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that the parties have been provided, although no decisions have been taken yet, with the new list of the exhibit numbers attributed to 92 bis material. I do understand that the Dzambasovic package appears under numbers P526 and then P526A, B, C, et cetera, up to and including P526M. If there is no -- if there are no objections, then this 92 bis material is admitted into evidence. The Chamber will receive a copy of the list made by the Registry soon. If there's any need to comment on the way these exhibits are described in that list, the Chamber would like to hear from the parties. If there are no comments in that respect, then they are not only admitted, but they will also appear on the list as you'll see the list. Then the next item is 7(b), Prosecution Exhibit 281. The Prosecution is expected to provide the redacted versions of P281 to all parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We have just done so, Your Honour. We've submitted that. And this, for clarity, should be under seal, given that this was a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P281, any objections by the Defence or --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then P281 is admitted, under seal. We move to our next agenda item, 7(c), which is Prosecution Exhibit 65, well, to say it short, it's Treanor evidence, binder 9A, tab 103. A revised copy would be submitted to the Chamber by the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We're doing so now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to the revised copy of this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We have it already, and there's no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, P65, binder 9A, tab 103, was already admitted. But then the originally submitted document is replaced by the revised edition and therefore is in evidence. Agenda item 7(d), P465. There, also, the OTP was supposed to provide the CD to all the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have the CD, and we've just provided it to the registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the Defence has received it also?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm not absolutely sure we've received it, Your Honour, but if we're receiving it now, we don't have a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There's no problem. Of course, to assess a CD on face value is not that easy because they look approximately the same. But P465, the CD, is now tendered into evidence, this version. Which brings us to agenda item 8, the three numbers that are already for a long time on the list, that is, P200, P202, and P203. The Office of the Prosecution was supposed to tender P200, including revised translations. Has that been done?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, let me report on 200, because there's different elements in respect of Prosecution Exhibit 200. In respect of 200-1, 200-8A, 200-8B, 200-9C, 200-27, 200-28, and 200-30, we're prepared to submit revised translations today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have they been provided already to the Defence before?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: They have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They have. Could we just -- because that's the first short list under 8(a), are there any objections against these revised translations?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the exhibits just mentioned, that is, all P numbers, 200-1, 200-8A, 200-8B, 200-9C, 200-27, 200-28, and 200-30 are admitted into evidence in their revised edition. Mr. Harmon, I interrupted you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, in respect of 200-4, there was a revision, I am told, by CLSS. We're prepared to submit the revision for 200-4. There was a memorandum that was prepared as well describing the revision. I'm not sure what the Trial Chamber wishes to do in respect of that memorandum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I did understand is that, on the 25th of February, the Defence informed the legal officer that it does not intend to pursue the translation issue any further.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, I think the memorandum -- when the parties agree that P200-4 is correctly translated, then nothing changes at this moment. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: With respect to 200-18E, the B/C/S version, it was my understanding that a more legible copy was to be submitted. We're prepared to submit a more legible copy today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any objections against the new, more legible version of P200-18E?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, there's no objection to greater legiblity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sometimes, if you see more, Ms. Loukas --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the old P200-18E is replaced by the new, more legible version. Then I think we've finally come to P200-31. That was already tendered by the Office of the Prosecution. I also understood that the issue of incorrect translations were indicated in an e-mail on the 26th of January.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, and I have a copy of that e-mail should that prove useful. But Ms. Javier is nodding her head. I assume she has a copy of the e-mail.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Due to an administrative error, we did not address that issue. We're prepared to do so this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we have dealt with all items under agenda item 8(a), but P200-31 is still pending so that the Prosecution has an opportunity to review the objections made by the Defence in respect of the translation of this document. Then we move to agenda item 8(b). These are P202 and 203. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It's my understanding, in respect of these two exhibits, Your Honour, that they have already been tendered. We are asking for their admission into evidence in their entirety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, there's no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then P202 and 203 are admitted into evidence. We move on to agenda item 9(a). We had not yet given any decision on the admission of the exhibits related to the testimony of Mr. Radic, and since there are no objections, as far as I understand, they are admitted into evidence. We move to agenda item 9(b). The previous interviews of Mr. Radic, the Chamber has indicated that it would admit them, if tendered, but we didn't receive anything until now. But I see that the Prosecution is tendering these interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. We're tendering the English and the B/C/S versions of each interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We already indicated that we would admit them, if tendered. Mr. Stewart, are there, nevertheless, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: There are no objections, Your Honour. But I had put into my hot little hands as I came into court a big pile of such items. I thought that I was tendering them, but I don't really mind who tenders them. I've got a big stack of Radic stuff here, if that helps anybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No, you're perfectly right. I overlooked that. It was the Defence who is tendering them. It doesn't make that much difference for the Chamber, as a matter of fact. But I now understand that the Prosecution has provided them but that the Defence has Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. tendered them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And they are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'd just like to get them off my table, if I might. I've got a set here for myself, and I've got three sets here which I assume are of practical use to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So may I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we do get a double series of --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: There are three sets, Your Honour, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps during the next break we could see, because just as you want them --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You don't want them, Your Honour, I think is what I'm hearing. So we'll sort it out, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that could be sorted out during the break so that we know. We need only one copy for each Judge and one copy for the Registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Your Honour. We'll sort that out. Might I just mention, while I'm on my feet --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
